policy: plan.json stays byte-identical, so the preregistered run's verdicts and its triggered overturn stand as recorded. Corrected rules run as compare --rules v2 on the same snapshot and are reported beside, never instead of, the preregistered result.

deviations.what: Which condition-6 closing print is the official close
deviations.plan_text: the day's closing-auction record with condition 6 (closing print)
deviations.ambiguity: Several exchanges can report a condition-6 print for the same symbol and day: 863 of 8,356 auction days in the snapshot have two or more, and 178 of those disagree on price. The plan did not say which exchange's print to take.
deviations.v1_implementation: the first condition-6 print from any exchange, often a small NYSE Arca (P) print listed before the listing exchange's cross
deviations.v2_rule: the condition-6 print on the listing exchange (the exchange of the day's condition-O opening records), taking the largest size when that exchange has several; else a condition-M print on the listing exchange; else the largest condition-6 print elsewhere (flagged closing_print_other_exchange); else the bar close
deviations.why_v2: the plan's own M rule is keyed to the listing (opening) exchange, which shows that the intended official close is the listing exchange's
deviations.effect: match/mismatch 535/137 (20.4%) under v1 becomes 589/84 (12.5%) under v2; the overturn triggers under both

deviations.v1_implementation: the relative change in the raw/split close ratio between the two dates must exceed 1e-6
deviations.why_v2: the provider's adjusted closes carry rounding noise of up to about 6e-4. 54 of the 57 v1 flags were noise; 3 were real splits (ELTX, QXO, UZX).
deviations.effect: split_between rows go from 57 to 3; the gain changes by at most about 0.06% relative, so verdicts are essentially unchanged

deviations.plan_text: Ticker_Used when present, else Ticker ... if that returns no event-date data: the alias-map Alias_Symbol
deviations.gap: When Ticker_Used differs from Ticker and has no event-date data, the original Ticker was never tried (OCTO 2025-09-08 was queried only as ORBS). The v1 snapshot never used its alias fallback: each event was tried under one symbol, and none of the 5 no-data events had an alias entry.
deviations.v2_rule: Ticker_Used, then Ticker if different, then the alias, fetched by audit.py supplement for events the snapshot has no event-date data for

deviations.what: Verdict naming for Status OK rows without a computed gain
deviations.v1_implementation: 10 Status OK rows have a blank Computed_Gain_Pct; 7 of them were named recovered_* although the package did have prices
deviations.v2_rule: those rows are package_uncomputed_match or package_uncomputed_mismatch
deviations.effect: recovered rows go from 274 to 267 plus 7 package_uncomputed rows
